A clear, evidence-informed stance

My work blends cognitive-behavioral techniques, trauma-sensitive practices, and relational approaches. I track progress collaboratively and adjust methods based on what the client finds helpful. Therapy is a shared process: I bring frameworks; you bring the lived experience.

Common myth vs. measured truth

Myth: Therapy fixes you quickly if you try hard enough.
Truth: Change is gradual and depends on consistent practice, safety, and realistic goals. I emphasize measurable steps and skill-building rather than promises.
Myth: You must disclose everything immediately.
Truth: You set the pace. Disclosure happens when it feels safe; I prioritize stabilization and consent over forcing narrative recounting.

Clinical boundaries & what I can help with

I provide therapy for anxiety, trauma symptoms, relationship challenges, major life transitions, and professional burnout. I do not provide emergency/crisis services. If you are in crisis, call local emergency services or a crisis line.

Confidentiality & scope

Sessions are confidential within legal and ethical boundaries. I will discuss limits to confidentiality, informed consent, and record-keeping during our first meeting.

Representative case notes (anonymized)

Case A — Transition & identity:

A person navigating a career change used structured behavioral experiments and values clarification to reduce avoidance and increase meaningful activity over 10 weeks.

Case B — Relationship patterns:

A couple learned reflective listening and boundary-setting to reduce reactive cycles; work included homework and skill practice between sessions.

Core practice pillars

  • Safety first — stabilization before processing.
  • Data-informed — symptom tracking and feedback.
  • Collaborative goals — measurable, testable steps.
  • Contextual sensitivity — attention to culture, identity, and systems.
Start a session
Payments: I offer a sliding scale and limited pro-bono options. Insurance submission guidance is available on request.

Questions people often ask

How long are sessions?
Standard sessions are 50 minutes. Extended or intensive sessions can be arranged when clinically appropriate.
Do you take insurance?
I provide superbills on request. Insurance acceptance varies; contact me for current details.
How quickly can I book?
Availability varies. New clients typically find an appointment within 1–3 weeks or sooner if there is an opening.

Areas of focus & clinical pathways

I work with adults using structured, skills-based strategies. Below are common presenting concerns and the program formats I typically offer.

Phone: {{PHONE}} • Email: {{EMAIL}}
{{PRIMARY_CTA_LABEL}}

Clinical specialties

Anxiety Disorders

Panic, generalized anxiety, health worry — evidence-based exposure and cognitive strategies to reduce avoidance and increase tolerance of uncertainty.

Trauma-Informed Care

Stabilization, safety-focused processing, and integration using titrated approaches; I prioritize pacing and consent.

Relationship Patterns

Communication repair, attachment patterns, and boundary work for individuals and partners (referrals for joint sessions when appropriate).

Life Transitions & Identity

Career shifts, becoming a parent, identity exploration — practical planning and values-aligned decision work.

Program formats — different frames for different goals

Focus Track (6–8 weeks)

Time-limited, targeted work for a specific problem (skill acquisition, behavioral experiments, in-session practice). Good for discrete goals and measurable change.

Foundations Program (12 weeks)

A block structured to build skills, deepen insight, and create sustainable routines. Includes periodic outcome checks and homework tailored to daily life.

Continuity Sessions (Ongoing)

Monthly or biweekly sessions for maintenance, life planning, or complex presentations. Flexible scheduling and periodic reviews.

Consult + Coaching Modules

Short consultations for clinicians or workplace referrals focusing on strategies to support wellbeing in team contexts (not therapy for all staff).

Anonymized case examples

Program: Focus Track

A client with situational panic used interoceptive exposure and cognitive restructuring across six sessions to reduce avoidance and regain daily functioning.

Program: Foundations

Work with someone experiencing chronic workplace stress included boundary development, sleep hygiene, and paced behavioral activation over 12 weeks with measurable improvements in routine and mood.

How I frame cost & access

Rather than flat tiers, I offer program frames with transparent expectations: session length, anticipated commitment, and a suggested range. I provide a sliding scale for limited slots and supply superbills for out-of-network reimbursement.

Check availability
Privacy & limitations: Notes are kept securely. Therapy is supportive care and not a substitute for emergency or medical services. In a crisis call emergency services or your local crisis number.

How I work: a hypothesis-driven, compassionate model

I treat therapy like testing an intervention: we form a hypothesis, try practical steps, measure change, and iterate. This keeps us grounded in what actually helps you in daily life.

Core phases of engagement

Assessment
— clear problem formulation, values, and target symptoms.
Intervention
— skills, behavioral experiments, pacing.
Measurement
— tracking outcomes, adjusting course.
Integration
— relapse prevention, community resources.

Evidence and flexibility

I prioritize approaches with empirical support (CBT, exposure, DBT skills, trauma-sensitive interventions) while adapting to your preferences, cultural context, and readiness. We test gently and respect pacing.

Myth vs. nuance

Myth: Clinicians always know the right answer.
Nuance: I bring frameworks and hypotheses; your feedback and real-world outcomes determine what we keep doing.
Myth: Therapy should make you feel better immediately.
Nuance: Sometimes progress is non-linear. Short-term discomfort can be part of long-term gains; we plan for stabilization and build safety nets.

Assessment tools I use

  • Validated symptom measures (brief questionnaires)
  • Behavioral tracking and exposure hierarchies
  • Collaborative progress reviews every 4–6 sessions

Session formats & candidacy

I offer standard 50-minute psychotherapy sessions, extended sessions by arrangement, and short consultations. Therapy is appropriate for non-emergency mental health concerns. For crisis support call emergency services.

Request an intake

Frequently asked

What makes this approach different?
It couples compassion with systematic measurement so we can see what helps and reduce guesswork.
How do you protect privacy?
Records are stored securely. I will review limits of confidentiality and informed consent at intake.
Can you work with my existing psychiatrist?
Yes. With your consent I coordinate care, focusing on psychotherapy while medication management remains with prescribers.
